detail.body:
# Description

Add an opt-in cuDNN OSS (FROST) forward provider for context-parallel attention. Supported D128 BF16 compact-THD causal training calls execute the complete compiled FROST forward chain through TE's common C++ dispatcher and return the packed FP32 Stats consumed by backward.

This draft is stacked on [#3699](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TransformerEngine/pull/3699) at `a7e91a56`. The current forward head is `a708a5a8`: [incremental diff](https://github.com/YangXu1990uiuc/TransformerEngine/compare/a7e91a561021374493671690009566af38a957d6...a708a5a83598053d49afd86e505413025f086007). It includes compatibility with the known FE prepared host signatures described below. The backward branch is unchanged. The combined GitHub diff includes that dependency until it lands.

## Execution and supported scope

- Python participates in cold preparation: construct the normal FE graph, select its supported forward engine, and retain the complete compiled host entry and immutable arguments. Steady-state C++ binds the current pointers, workspace and stream and calls TVM-FFI directly. The compiled entry includes metadata/remap, descriptor setup and the main SDPA kernel.
- Support SM100, D128, BF16 training, separate Q/K/V, compact THD, top-left causal padding, and no dropout, bias, sinks, paging or sliding window. Stats remain packed token-major FP32 natural logarithms.
- Compactness is an explicit promise checked on the GPU every execution, including graph replay: physical origins must equal zero-based cumulative lengths, with valid bounds and nonempty KV for live Q. Unequal sequence lengths are supported; there is no dense conversion. Physical storage holes, AllGather forward subcalls with those holes, D256 forward and noncausal forward are outside this initial scope.
- Cache plans per declaration/device without holding a C++ cache lock across Python. Validate current operand/workspace alignment, capacity and overlap. Retain immutable FFI values in the cache without adding FFI array-type registration dependencies to the common library.
- Add default-off, fallback and strict modes, documentation, seventeen directed forward tests and 25 CPU contract tests. The dedicated FROST QA target requires all 104 tests and all twelve isolated metadata-guard children.
- Accept only the known 27-, 31- and 37-slot FE host signatures. Extra score, bias and KV-mask slots must contain their exact disabled defaults. Unknown signatures and enabled unsupported features are rejected. C++ uses bounded stack storage and passes the actual argument count, retaining native steady-state execution.

The integration selects existing FE kernels; it does not change their arithmetic or communication implementation. The separate private backward exp2 experiment is not part of this PR.

## Use and dependencies

Build TE with CuTeDSL support and install compatible FE source, `nvidia-cutlass-dsl[cu13]>=4.8.0`, and `apache-tvm-ffi`. This draft validates and consumes FE's private prepared forward metadata. A stable FE export contract and compatible dependency packaging remain prerequisites for graduating the integration.

Current-FE directed requalification used develop `7701e232` plus [FE #1690](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1690), the terminal dQ-credit synchronization repair in [FE #1698](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1698), and an isolated FP32 padding-helper correction. This is a composed qualification package, not unmodified develop or the unmodified published FE heads. Ordinary numerical tests do not detect the unrepaired D128 dense/THD barrier-phase violation. The current package passes the directed TE suite and unfiltered terminal-credit synccheck; the FE performance holds remain in force. The current-head 2K and 8K CP comparisons below use this package and explicitly exclude #1696 and #1702. Older comparisons retain their earlier frozen dependency versions.

```bash
export NVTE_ENABLE_CUTEDSL_BACKEND=1
export CUDNN_FRONTEND_ENABLE_FROST_ENGINES=1
export NVTE_FUSED_ATTN=1
export NVTE_FLASH_ATTN=0
export NVTE_FUSED_ATTN_FROST_FWD=2          # strict; 1 permits backend fallback
export NVTE_FUSED_ATTN_FROST_FWD_COMPACT=1  # only for the documented layout
export NVTE_FUSED_ATTN_FROST=2             # optional: pair with OSS backward
```

Warm up each declaration before CUDA Graph capture. Leave the compactness promise disabled for physical holes or unsupported declarations. `NVTE_FUSED_ATTN_FROST_FWD=0` retains the existing forward route.

The historical CP measurements below used FE develop `2bcdd1bb` plus [#1696](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1696) for the forward lookup optimization and the complete [#1690](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1690) patch for the existing D256 pitched-backward regressions. The D256 pitch dependency is not required by the D128 forward implementation itself.

## Current compatibility validation

The original current-develop run passed 62 backward cases, then rejected the first forward declaration because FE's host signature had grown beyond the fixed 27-slot bridge. The repair updates both Python export and the native frame while keeping unsupported optional features disabled.

- **25 CPU contract tests pass:** legacy/current signatures, neutral optional slots, malformed or unknown signatures, and retained feature guards.
- **79/79 original TE GPU tests pass, zero failures/errors/skips**, on an exclusive production B200 (148 SM, 1000 W) with cuDNN 9.27.0.42, CUDA 13.2 and the dependency package above. This includes all twelve isolated metadata guards, independent CPU-FP64 O/Stats/gradient comparisons, rebinding, streams, changed-length replay and cached execution with Python preparation callbacks disabled. The native forward plans use the current 37-slot host signature.
- **Eight terminal-credit FE regressions pass ordinarily and all eight pass under unfiltered synccheck with zero reported errors.** No unexpected GPU process was observed. This is directed synchronization coverage, not a complete sanitizer matrix.
- Recompiled the changed common CUDA unit with the existing CUDA 13.2 configuration, linked with 113 hash-verified unchanged parent objects, and loaded that library through the normal current-head TE/PyTorch path. The submitted native code matches the tested code; Python preparation differs only by an AST-equivalent trailing-comma formatting fix.
- Changed-file pre-commit, Pylint 3.3.1, C++ lint and diff checks pass. The QA launcher now includes the 25 contract tests; the reported CPU and GPU suites were run separately.

The current-head complete-CP comparison below exposes a forward-path slowdown. Isolated host-submission and device-runtime attribution for this combination remains pending. The PR remains a draft pending that investigation, current-head review/CI, remaining integration qualification and the dependency holds.

## Current-head D128 2K complete CP comparison — hold

Published TE head `a708a5a8`, through the actual native C++ execution route, now completes the comparison with the current composed FE package described above: develop `7701e232` + #1690 + the full #1698 synchronization repair + the isolated FP32 padding-helper correction. **This package excludes the held #1696 forward lookup optimization and #1702.** The separate terminal-credit wait-overlap candidate is also absent.

Workload: **B256/S2048/Hq32/Hkv8/D128, BF16 causal compact THD, 524288 tokens, CP4/A2A**. Four production B200 GPUs (148 SM, default 1000 W) use cuDNN 9.27.0.42 and CUDA 13.2-built TE. All arms share the TE source and communication implementation. Warm eager latency includes forward, backward, helpers and communication, reporting the slowest rank; prepared Python callbacks are disabled during timing.

| Provider | Median complete-CP latency |
| --- | ---: |
| cuDNN backend | 25.829 ms |
| FROST backward; cuDNN forward | 24.329 ms |
| FROST forward and backward | 28.411 ms |
| FlashAttention 4 | 25.462 ms |

Median paired latency changes across four balanced orders:

- Backward-only / FA4: **-4.44%**, faster in 4/4 orders.
- Combined / backward-only: **+16.77%**, slower in 4/4 orders.
- Combined / cuDNN backend: **+10.00%**.
- Combined / FA4: **+11.59%**.

All **256 complete O/dQ/dK/dV comparisons**, 64 fresh workers and 48 timing windows pass (maximum relative RMS 0.003662). Telemetry/stability gates pass and no foreign GPU process is observed. Peak allocated memory is 15,604,025,856 bytes for native and 13,976,506,368 bytes for either FROST arm; preserved nanobind shutdown leak warnings remain undiagnosed, so this does not qualify lifetime or leak behavior.

**Hold for forward performance attribution.** The previous favorable 2K results below included #1696 and used different frozen FE versions. This comparison does not isolate the TE ABI repair as the cause. The missing bounded THD lookup is a candidate explanation requiring a controlled comparison; #1696 itself remains held for its separate small-batch regression. This result does not qualify a merge, establish an original-324-grid win rate, or measure the private wait-overlap candidate.

## Current-head D128 8K complete CP comparison — hold

The same published TE `a708a5a8` and frozen FE package used for the 2K result above also complete **B64/S8192/Hq32/Hkv8/D128, BF16 causal compact THD, 524288 tokens, CP4/A2A**. This still excludes #1696, #1702 and the private terminal-credit wait-overlap candidate. Hardware, native C++ execution, communication, callback-free timing and measurement definitions match the 2K comparison.

| Provider | Median complete-CP latency |
| --- | ---: |
| cuDNN backend | 48.569 ms |
| FROST backward; cuDNN forward | 45.464 ms |
| FROST forward and backward | 46.296 ms |
| FlashAttention 4 | 44.451 ms |

Across the four balanced orders, the median paired latency changes are:

- Backward-only / FA4: **+2.35%**, slower in 4/4 orders.
- Combined / backward-only: **+1.73%**, slower in 4/4 orders.
- Combined / cuDNN backend: **-4.64%**, faster in 4/4 orders.
- Combined / FA4: **+4.05%**, slower in 4/4 orders.

All **256 complete O/dQ/dK/dV comparisons**, 64 fresh workers and 48 timing windows pass; maximum relative RMS is 0.003660. Telemetry/stability and full-node isolation gates pass. Peak allocated memory is 15,604,026,880 bytes for native and 13,976,603,648 bytes for combined FROST; this is not a lifetime/leak qualification.

**Forward remains on hold.** Enabling it adds 1.73% here, compared with 16.77% at B256/S2048. Batch and sequence length both changed, so this is evidence of workload dependence, not isolated attribution to the lookup algorithm. A bounded-lookup candidate that preserves the B=1 specialization is undergoing separate production qualification; it is absent from both current CP measurements. Neither measurement qualifies a merge or establishes an original-324-grid win rate.

<summary>Historical dependency-specific validation and CP measurements</summary>

## Historical validation and CP measurements

On production B200 (148 SM), cuDNN 9.27.0.42, CUDA 13.2-built TE, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130 and CuTeDSL 4.8 with its CUDA 13 compiler:

- Recompiled the changed common CUDA units and linked them with hash-verified unchanged build objects; no undefined link symbols were added or removed. A fresh FE binding is used. Native source snapshots match the historical `020ed08b` implementation after whitespace-only formatting.
- **79/79 directed tests pass, zero skips:** seventeen new forward cases and 62 backward regressions, including all twelve isolated device-metadata guards. Coverage includes independent CPU FP64 O/Stats/gradient checks, MHA/GQA, unequal lengths, changed bindings and streams, changed-input/length and empty-to-live graph replay, and cached execution with Python preparation callbacks disabled.
- Changed-file pre-commit and diff checks pass at `020ed08b`.
- Follow-up `11aab95c` resolves the new Python lint findings: dict literal spelling, redundant parentheses, an unused parameter name, and scoped annotations for explicit ABI checks/compiled CUDA bindings. Pylint 3.3.1 and changed-file hooks pass locally. A normalized AST comparison verifies equivalent preparation code; the native binaries, kernel and GPU qualification remain attributed to `020ed08b`. [Equivalence evidence](https://sc.talos.nvidia.com/view/home/scratch.yanxu_libs/cudnn_frontend/.te-cp-20261012/results/te_forward_v202_lint_equivalence.json). GitHub checks subsequently passed for that historical head.

[Native qualification and exact source/binary evidence](https://sc.talos.nvidia.com/view/home/scratch.yanxu_libs/cudnn_frontend/.te-cp-20261012/results/te_frost_forward_v197_qualified.json) · [Native link audit](https://sc.talos.nvidia.com/view/home/scratch.yanxu_libs/cudnn_frontend/.te-cp-20261012/results/te_frost_forward_v195_native_link_audit.json).

A complete **CP4/A2A** comparison now passes on four B200 GPUs: B256 × S2048, Hq32/Hkv8, D128 BF16 causal compact THD, 524288 total tokens. All arms use the same TE source and communication implementation. Warm eager timing includes forward, backward and communication and reports the slowest rank's host elapsed time.

| Provider | Median total latency |
| --- | ---: |
| cuDNN backend | 25.762 ms |
| FROST backward; cuDNN forward | 24.241 ms |
| FROST forward and backward | 24.063 ms |
| FlashAttention 4 | 25.452 ms |

Adding forward to the FROST backward path reduces complete-CP latency by **0.73%**. The combined path reduces latency by **6.60%** versus cuDNN and **5.45%** versus FA4. Percentages are medians of four per-round paired ratios; all four orders favor the combined path. This is one coordinate on one node, using the FE dependencies above, and is not an original-324-grid win-rate claim or a projection to longer sequences/other communication types.

Four balanced process orders comprise sixteen fresh four-rank sets, 64 workers and 48 timing windows. All **256 full O/dQ/dK/dV comparisons** pass (maximum relative RMS 0.003662); power, HBM-clock, temperature and stability checks pass. Untimed route/fill audits verify native backward in both FROST arms, engine 20511 only in the combined arm, and no redundant gradient-output fills. GPU evidence is attributed to `020ed08b`; `11aab95c` has the equivalent Python preparation spelling described above. [Complete CP measurements, route checks and raw hashes](https://sc.talos.nvidia.com/view/home/scratch.yanxu_libs/cudnn_frontend/.te-cp-20261012/results/te_frost_forward_cp_v199_qualified.json).


The same four-arm protocol also completes at **B64 × S8192**, retaining 524288 tokens, CP4/A2A, Hq32/Hkv8, D128 BF16 causal compact THD and the same FE dependencies. All four arms run on one B200 node; the 2K experiment above ran on a different node.

| Provider | Median total latency at 8K |
| --- | ---: |
| cuDNN backend | 48.143 ms |
| FROST backward; cuDNN forward | 45.230 ms |
| FROST forward and backward | 45.043 ms |
| FlashAttention 4 | 44.143 ms |

At 8K, adding forward changes complete-CP latency by **-0.33%** relative to backward alone. The combined path changes latency by **-6.44%** versus cuDNN and **+1.90%** versus FA4; backward alone is **+2.51%** versus FA4. Negative means lower latency. Ratios are paired within each of four balanced orders. The combined path is faster than FA4 in 0/4 orders, and adding forward improves on backward alone in 4/4 orders.

The 2K advantage does not extend to this 8K coordinate: the integrated path still trails FA4. This PR provides native execution of the supported OSS forward chain; it does not establish a universal performance advantage.

The 8K run passes another **256 full O/dQ/dK/dV comparisons** (maximum relative RMS 0.003660), with 64 fresh workers and all 48 timing windows passing the predeclared telemetry/stability checks. Native route, source/binary identity and output-fill checks pass. No private backward kernel experiment is used in either CP comparison, and no original-324-grid wins are added. [Complete 8K CP evidence](https://sc.talos.nvidia.com/view/home/scratch.yanxu_libs/cudnn_frontend/.te-cp-20261012/results/te_frost_forward_cp_v204_qualified.json).

An earlier attempt stopped at native-control TCPStore initialization with `EADDRINUSE`, before that worker executed attention. Its partial timings remain excluded. The successful repeat uses a unique file rendezvous with an otherwise unchanged attention/timing body. [Retained startup diagnostic](https://sc.talos.nvidia.com/view/home/scratch.yanxu_libs/cudnn_frontend/.te-cp-20261012/results/te_frost_forward_cp_v196_failure.json).

The first native QA run also exposed a dependency-snapshot assembly error: the D256 pitch patch had been skipped. That failure is retained; after verifying the applied dependency files, the complete 79-case repeat passed. [Dependency diagnostic](https://sc.talos.nvidia.com/view/home/scratch.yanxu_libs/cudnn_frontend/.te-cp-20261012/results/te_frost_forward_v195_dependency_diagnostic.json).

Full GPU L0, JAX execution and a clean sanitizer qualification for this new bridge remain pending. The dedicated CI target still requires owner provisioning/enrollment. This remains a draft pending those integration decisions and maintainer review.

[Rolling explanation and evidence](https://sc.talos.nvidia.com/view/home/scratch.yanxu_libs/cudnn_frontend/.te-cp-20261012/explainer-20261014/context-parallel-optimizations.en.html).

## Follow-up D128 kernel synchronization qualification

[cuDNN Frontend #1698](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1698) repairs terminal dQ barrier-phase reuse in the dense and THD FROST D128 backward kernels, including the grouped-query routes. Its exact-source regression reproduces pre-fix Missing wait reports and passes 70 ordinary tests plus all eight cases under each of racecheck and synccheck after the repair. Unfiltered memcheck qualification remains pending because of a retained CUDA runtime-recompilation API warning.

The complete-CP timings above remain attributed to their stated FE/kernel snapshots, before this repair. Repaired 8K and 2K CP4/A2A remeasurements are reported separately below; the full current-FE package remains outside that qualification. [Repair validation and limitations](https://sc.talos.nvidia.com/view/home/scratch.yanxu_libs/cudnn_frontend/.te-cp-20261012/results/frost_credit_pr_v295_result.json).

## Repaired D128 8K complete CP remeasurement

A new complete CP4/A2A run uses the qualified packed terminal-credit repair, AST-equivalent to [FE #1698](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1698), on the frozen FE197 integration with #1696 and #1690. Only that packed kernel changes; TE native binaries, all other FE inputs and communication remain identical across the four providers. This is a new comparison with the repaired dependency, not a measurement of repair overhead against an unrepaired arm.

Workload: **B64/S8192/Hq32/Hkv8/D128, BF16 causal compact THD, 524288 tokens, CP4/A2A**. Four production B200 GPUs use 148 SMs, default 1000 W limits and NV18 links; cuDNN 9.27.0.42, CUDA 13.2-built TE, CuTeDSL 4.8 cu13, FA4 `4.0.0b35.dev1+gbb25ba3`. Warm eager timing includes forward, backward, helpers and communication and reports the slowest rank.

| Provider | Median complete-CP latency |
| --- | ---: |
| cuDNN backend | 48.132 ms |
| FROST backward; cuDNN forward | 45.110 ms |
| FROST forward and backward | 44.823 ms |
| FlashAttention 4 | 43.759 ms |

Paired latency changes: backward-only/FA4 **+3.03%**; combined/FA4 **+2.30%**; combined/backward-only **-0.81%**; combined/cuDNN **-6.88%**. Negative means lower latency. Percentages are medians of four paired round ratios. The combined path is faster than FA4 in **0/4** orders.

All **256 complete output/gradient comparisons**, 64 fresh workers and 48 timing windows pass, with maximum relative RMS 0.003660. Actual packed-GQA backward route, forward engine, source/binary hashes, output-fill audits and telemetry/stability gates are checked. A separately versioned collector corrects only an expected worker-status spelling; the frozen workloads, measurements and all admission gates are unchanged.

This is one coordinate on one node, not an original-grid win rate or full qualification of the current FE package. The earlier results retain their own frozen-source attribution; the repaired 2K remeasurement follows below. Public current-upstream memcheck and the remaining integration graduation requirements above remain pending. [Repaired CP qualification](https://sc.talos.nvidia.com/view/home/scratch.yanxu_libs/cudnn_frontend/.te-cp-20261012/results/te_frost_forward_cp_v299_qualified.json) · [Collector correction](https://sc.talos.nvidia.com/view/home/scratch.yanxu_libs/cudnn_frontend/.te-cp-20261012/results/te_frost_forward_cp_v299_collector_correction.json).

## Repaired D128 2K complete CP remeasurement

The same repaired FE dependency and unchanged TE binaries now complete the four-provider comparison at **B256/S2048/Hq32/Hkv8/D128, BF16 causal compact THD, 524288 tokens, CP4/A2A**. The dependency is frozen FE197 + #1696/#1690 with the qualified packed terminal-credit repair, AST-equivalent to [FE #1698](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1698). All providers use the same TE communication implementation.

Four production B200 GPUs use 148 SMs, default 1000 W and NV18 links; cuDNN 9.27.0.42, CUDA 13.2-built TE, CuTeDSL 4.8 cu13, FA4 `4.0.0b35.dev1+gbb25ba3`. Warm eager latency includes forward, backward, helpers and communication and reports the slowest rank. This coordinate runs on a different node from the repaired 8K result above.

| Provider | Median complete-CP latency |
| --- | ---: |
| cuDNN backend | 26.017 ms |
| FROST backward; cuDNN forward | 24.493 ms |
| FROST forward and backward | 24.287 ms |
| FlashAttention 4 | 25.559 ms |

Paired latency changes: backward-only/FA4 **-4.16%**; combined/FA4 **-5.01%**; combined/backward-only **-0.83%**; combined/cuDNN **-6.69%**. Negative means lower latency. These are medians of four paired round ratios; all four orders favor the combined path for every comparison.

All **256 complete output/gradient comparisons**, 64 fresh workers and 48 timing windows pass (maximum relative RMS 0.003662). Actual packed-GQA backward and forward routes, source/binary hashes, output-fill audits, hardware telemetry and timing stability are checked.

The repaired 2K and 8K results establish gains at these two bounded coordinates; 8K remains 2.30% slower than FA4. They do not establish an original-324-grid win rate, measure repair overhead against an unrepaired arm, or qualify the entire current FE package. Earlier D256 measurements retain their stated source versions. Stable FE export/packaging, public current-upstream memcheck and the remaining integration qualification remain pending. [Repaired 2K qualification and frozen evidence](https://sc.talos.nvidia.com/view/home/scratch.yanxu_libs/cudnn_frontend/.te-cp-20261012/results/te_frost_forward_cp_v304_qualified.json).

</details>

## Follow-up causal THD forward kernel optimization

[cuDNN Frontend #1702](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1702), head `41be3b14`, builds on #1696 and moves one quarter of softmax exp2 work on eligible SM100 BF16 D128-flavor causal THD **interior** tiles to the existing FMA implementation. Masked/diagonal tiles retain MUFU; paged, split-KV, sliding-window and FP16 causal paths are excluded. This is a separate FROST kernel change; the TE dispatch code and this PR's head are unchanged.

At **B32/S16384/Hq32/Hkv8/D128, BF16 causal THD, 524288 tokens, CP4/A2A**, two independent B200 nodes show **1.46–1.72% lower complete-CP latency** against the repaired FROST forward+backward baseline. Timing includes forward, backward, helpers and communication, with identical TE binaries and communication, four balanced orders, 256 full output/gradient checks and 48 telemetry/stability windows per node. Baseline/candidate/FA4 medians are **74.617/73.342/70.940 ms** on one node and **74.517/73.367/70.716 ms** on the other. Paired ratios are analyzed separately per node; the optimized path still takes **3.34–3.78% longer than FA4**.

The published forward source independently passes **22 numerical/replay cases plus one public-layout rejection** on B200, with **two cases under each of memcheck, racecheck and synccheck**, zero errors/hazards. Tests include both packed Stats layouts, changed-length replay and smaller/asymmetric D128-envelope widths. The original complete-CP measurements retain their frozen experimental-package attribution; they do not remeasure the entire new public FE package or add an original-grid win rate. Existing TE integration/export/packaging requirements remain unchanged.

[Two-node complete-CP comparison](https://sc.talos.nvidia.com/view/home/scratch.yanxu_libs/cudnn_frontend/.te-cp-20261012/explainer-20261014/context-parallel-optimizations.en.html#forward-repeat-v213) · [Published kernel qualification](https://sc.talos.nvidia.com/view/home/scratch.yanxu_libs/cudnn_frontend/.te-cp-20261012/results/frost_exp25_public_v353_result.json).

+def _case(dim, thd, unequal, causal, seed=31, bottom_right=False, kv_length=None, q_length=None):
+    generator = torch.Generator(device="cpu").manual_seed(seed)
+    q_lengths, k_lengths = ((129, 63), (193, 97)) if unequal else ((128, 128), (256, 256))
+    if q_length is not None:
+        assert not unequal
+        q_lengths = (q_length, q_length)
+    if kv_length is not None:
+        assert not unequal
+        k_lengths = (kv_length, kv_length)
+    heads, kv_heads = 4, 1
+    inputs, expected = [], []
+    for sq, sk in zip(q_lengths, k_lengths):
+
+        def draw(s, h):
+            return (torch.randn(s, h, dim, generator=generator) * 0.5).bfloat16()
+
+        q, k, v, do = draw(sq, heads), draw(sk, kv_heads), draw(sk, kv_heads), draw(sq, heads)
+        qr, kr, vr = (x.double().transpose(0, 1).requires_grad_() for x in (q, k, v))
+        scores = (qr @ kr.repeat_interleave(heads // kv_heads, 0).transpose(-1, -2)) * dim**-0.5
+        if causal:
+            scores = scores.masked_fill(
+                torch.arange(sk)[None, :]
+                > torch.arange(sq)[:, None] + (sk - sq if bottom_right else 0),
+                -torch.inf,
+            )
+        # Bottom-right Q > KV has keyless leading rows: their output/gradient is zero.
+        keyless = torch.isneginf(scores).all(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
+        probabilities = scores.masked_fill(keyless, 0).softmax(-1).masked_fill(keyless, 0)
+        result = probabilities @ vr.repeat_interleave(heads // kv_heads, 0)
+        grads = torch.autograd.grad(result, (qr, kr, vr), do.transpose(0, 1).double())
+        inputs.append((q, k, v, do))
+        expected.append(tuple(x.transpose(0, 1).detach() for x in grads))
+    combine = torch.cat if thd else torch.stack
+    q, k, v, do = (combine([row[i] for row in inputs]).cuda() for i in range(4))
+    reference = tuple(combine([row[i] for row in expected]) for i in range(3))
+    prefixes = [
+        torch.tensor([0, lengths[0], sum(lengths)], device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
+        for lengths in (q_lengths, k_lengths)
+    ]
+    return q, k, v, do, prefixes, reference, max(q_lengths), max(k_lengths)
+
+
+def _calls(case, dim, thd, causal, bottom_right=False, origins=None):
+    from transformer_engine.pytorch.cpp_extensions.fused_attn import (
+        FusedAttnBackend,
+        fused_attn_fwd,
+        fused_attn_bwd,
+    )
+
+    q, k, v, do, (cu_q, cu_kv), reference, sq, sk = case
+    fmt = "thd" if thd else "bshd"
+    mask = (
+        ("padding_causal" if causal else "padding") if thd else ("causal" if causal else "no_mask")
+    )
+    if bottom_right:
+        assert causal
+        mask += "_bottom_right"
+    options = dict(
+        max_seqlen_q=sq,
+        max_seqlen_kv=sk,
+        cu_seqlens_q=cu_q,
+        cu_seqlens_kv=cu_kv,
+        q=q,
+        k=k,
+        v=v,
+        fake_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+        fused_attention_backend=FusedAttnBackend.F16_arbitrary_seqlen,
+        cu_seqlens_q_padded=cu_q if origins is None else origins[0],
+        cu_seqlens_kv_padded=cu_kv if origins is None else origins[1],
+        attn_scale=dim**-0.5,
+        qkv_layout="_".join([fmt] * 3),
+        o_format=fmt,
+        attn_mask_type=mask,
+        dropout=0.0,
+    )
+    o, aux = fused_attn_fwd(is_training=True, **options)

+        return fused_attn_bwd(

+            d_o=do,
+            aux_ctx_tensors=aux,
+            do_format=fmt,
+            dqkv_layout=options["qkv_layout"],
+            deterministic=False,
+            **options
+        )[:3]
+
+    return backward, reference

+def _pitched_case(cp, sk, seed=31):
+    """Full THD buffers with the physical origins of a causal AllGather step."""
+    case = _case(256, True, False, True, seed, bottom_right=True, kv_length=sk)
+    q, k, v, do, prefixes, reference, sq, _ = case
+    pq, pk = 2 * sq, 2 * cp * sq
+    origin = sq if sk > pk // 2 else 0
+
+    def expand(value, kv, fill):
+        pitch, length, start = (pk, sk, 0) if kv else (pq, sq, origin)
+        heads, dim = value.shape[1:]
+        full = torch.full((2, pitch, heads, dim), fill, device=value.device, dtype=value.dtype)
+        full[:, start : start + length].copy_(value.view(2, length, heads, dim))

+"""Prepare cuDNN OSS backward plans for TE's native dispatcher.
+
+Only preparation enters Python. The registry entry is the compiled TVM-FFI

+from functools import partial
+from importlib.metadata import PackageNotFoundError, version
+import logging
+
+_LOG = logging.getLogger("transformer_engine.frost")
+_OWNERS = {}
+_ROLES = ("q", "k", "v", "o", "do", "stats", "dq", "dk", "dv")
+_ORIGIN_ROLES = ("q", "k", "v", "o", "do", "dq", "dk", "dv", "stats")
+_POINTER_ROLES = _ROLES + ("seq_q", "seq_kv") + tuple("ragged_" + r for r in _ORIGIN_ROLES)
+_ENGINES = {128: 20609, 256: 20607}

+def _declarations(batch, heads, kv_heads, sq, sk, dim, tq, thd, q_pitch=0, kv_pitch=0):
+    """Logical BHSD declarations over TE's BSHD or packed token-major storage."""
+    result = {}
+    for role in _ROLES:
+        kv = role in ("k", "v", "dk", "dv")
+        h, s = (kv_heads, sk) if kv else (heads, sq)
+        if role == "stats":
+            shape = (batch, heads, sq, 1)
+            stride = (tq * heads, 1, heads, 1) if thd else (heads * sq, sq, 1, 1)
+        else:
+            pitch = (kv_pitch if kv else q_pitch) or s
+            shape, stride = (batch, h, s, dim), (pitch * h * dim, dim, h * dim, 1)
+        result[role] = (shape, stride)
+    return result
+

+def _native_metadata(spec, dim, thd, expected_prefix):
+    """Refuse an unfamiliar prepared ABI instead of dropping optional operands."""
+    from cudnn.frost.compiled_cache import positional_entry
+    import tvm_ffi
+
+    if (
+        spec.name != f"sdpa_bwd_sm100_d{dim}"
+        or spec.scale_log2
+        or spec.packed_tile_groups
+        or bool(spec.length_form) != thd
+    ):
+        raise RuntimeError("Unsupported cuDNN OSS prepared backward contract")
+    roles = tuple(spec.roles)
+    expected = _POINTER_ROLES if thd else _ROLES + (("seq_kv", "delta") if dim == 256 else ())
+    if roles != expected or len(spec.operands) != len(roles):
+        raise RuntimeError(f"Unsupported cuDNN OSS operand order: {roles}")
+    native = positional_entry(spec.artifact.entry)
+    if not isinstance(native, tvm_ffi.Function):
+        raise RuntimeError("cuDNN OSS must expose a compiled native TVM-FFI entry")

+            raise RuntimeError("Unsupported cuDNN OSS packed backward prefix")
+    elif expected_prefix:
+        raise RuntimeError("Dense backward cannot have a packed prefix")

+    metadata.extend(expected_prefix)
+    for role, operand in zip(roles, spec.operands):
+        if operand is None:
+            metadata.extend((-1, 0, 1))
+            continue
+        if role not in _POINTER_ROLES or operand.opaque_bytes or operand.packed_tile_bytes:

+        if role in ("seq_q", "seq_kv"):
+            span += 4  # TE supplies B+1 cumulative lengths, lens_form=3.
+        if span <= 0 or span > 2**63 - 1:
+            raise RuntimeError("cuDNN OSS operand byte span is not representable")

+            name=name + "_origin",
+            dim=[batch + 1, 1, 1, 1],

+        graph.tensor(
+            name="cu_" + role,
+            dim=[batch + 1, 1, 1, 1],
+            stride=[1, 1, 1, 1],
+            data_type=cudnn.data_type.INT32,
+        )
+        for role in ("q", "kv")

+        generate_stats=True,
+        attn_scale=scale,
+        use_padding_mask=True,
+        use_causal_mask=True,

+        cu_seq_len_kv=lengths[1],

+        [sq * heads * 128, 128, heads * 128, 1]
+    )

+// Default-off output initialization policy. The framework may omit output initialization
+// only under this same predicate used by common dispatch. Strict mode prevents
+// native fallback; common dispatch validates the device lengths/origins on every
+// execution before FROST writes all rows. Pitched and unequal layouts keep zeros.
+inline bool frost_d128_compact_outputs(NVTE_QKV_Layout qkv, NVTE_QKV_Layout dqkv, NVTEDType dtype,
+                                       size_t dq, size_t dv, size_t batch, size_t tq, size_t tk,
+                                       size_t sq, size_t sk, size_t hq, size_t hkv) {
+  return getenv<int>("NVTE_FUSED_ATTN_FROST") == 2 &&
+         getenv<bool>("NVTE_FUSED_ATTN_FROST_D128_NOZERO") && qkv == NVTE_THD_THD_THD &&
+         dqkv == qkv && dtype == kNVTEBFloat16 && dq == 128 && dv == 128 && batch > 0 && sq > 0 &&
+         sq == sk && sq % 128 == 0 && tq % batch == 0 && tk % batch == 0 && tq / batch == sq &&
+         tk / batch == sk && hkv > 0 && hq > hkv && hq % hkv == 0;
